title: Temurah 18
description: The Gemara finishes asking what “only” and “it is” exclude, then turns to the mishna’s dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis over whether a peace offering’s offspring is sacrificed, with Rabbi Pappeyas’s testimony, the thanks offering’s offspring that need no loaves, and Rabbi Elazar on the male born to a female set aside as a burnt offering.
topics: 🐏 What Rabbi Yishmael’s “only” excludes: a positive mitzva for one who sacrifices anyway
🌾 Rav Huna: a guilt offering consigned to grazing, slaughtered unspecified, is valid as a burnt offering
🚶 “You shall take and go”: even from their pasture, or from their threshing
🐄 Is the offspring of a peace offering sacrificed? Rabbi Eliezer’s decree and Rabbi Pappeyas’s cow
👶 The offspring of the offspring: Rabba against Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and Rabbi Ḥiyya’s “lamb”
📅 Eaten on Passover, its offspring on “the Festival”: Sukkot or Shavuot?
🍞 A thanks offering’s offspring and substitute: thanks offerings without the loaves
🔥 The male born to a female burnt offering: graze and be sold, or sacrificed itself, as Rabbi Elazar says?

a1.he: אִי דְּאָשָׁם — גְּמִירִי לַהּ דְּלִרְעִיָּיה אָזְלָא, דְּכֹל שֶׁבַּחַטָּאת מֵתָה בָּאָשָׁם רוֹעֶה. לְעוֹלָם בְּחַטָּאת, וְהִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ לְמִיתָה, וּקְרָא לְמַעוֹטֵי לְהַקְרָבָה.

a2.he: וְהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא, כֵּיוָן דִּלְמִיתָה אָזְלָא — מִמֵּילָא לָא קָרְבָה! אֶלָּא הִלְכְתָא לְחַטָּאת, וְקָרָא לְמַעוֹטֵי תְּמוּרַת אָשָׁם.

a3.he: הָא נָמֵי הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ, דְּאָמְרִי: כֹּל שֶׁבַּחַטָּאת מֵתָה, בָּאָשָׁם רוֹעֶה. אֶלָּא קְרָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, דְּאִי עָבַר וּמַקְרֵיב — קָאֵי בַּעֲשֵׂה.

a4.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ כּוּ׳. הוּא קָרֵב וְאֵין תְּמוּרָתוֹ קְרֵיבָה. לְמָה לִי קְרָא, וְהָא הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לָהּ!

a5.he: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא קְרָא לְמָה לִי? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אָשָׁם שֶׁנִּיתַּק לִרְעִיָּיה וּשְׁחָטוֹ סְתָם — כָּשֵׁר לְשֵׁם עוֹלָה.

a6.he: נִיתַּק — אִין, לֹא נִיתַּק — לָא. מַאי טַעְמָא? הוּא — בַּהֲוָויָיתוֹ יְהֵא.

a7.he: וּלְהַאי תַּנָּא דְּקָא יָלֵיף מֵהָנֵי קְרָאֵי, תִּיפּוֹק לִי מִ״זָּכָר״ וּ״נְקֵבָה״? הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִוְלַד בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין, וְלִתְמוּרַת בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין.

a8.he: וְתִיפּוֹק לִי כּוּלְּהוּ מֵהַאי קְרָא? ״אִם״ לָא מַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ.

a9.he: וּלְהַאי תַּנָּא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״זָּכָר״ ״אִם נְקֵבָה״, תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ מָה עָבֵיד לְהוּ! אֲפִילּוּ מִמִּירְעַיְיהוּ. לִישָּׁנָא אַחְרִינָא: מִמּוֹרִגַּיְיהוּ.

a10.he: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: וְלַד שְׁלָמִים לֹא יִקְרַב שְׁלָמִים, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יִקְרַב.

a11.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ עַל וְלַד וְלַד שְׁלָמִים, וְעַל וְלַד וְלַד תְּמוּרָה שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרַב. עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ? עַל הַוָּלָד, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִקְרַב, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יִקְרַב.

a12.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי פַּפְּיָיס עַל וְלַד שְׁלָמִים שֶׁיִּקְרַב שְׁלָמִים. אָמַר רַבִּי פַּפְּיָיס: אֲנִי מֵעִיד שֶׁהָיְתָה לָנוּ פָּרָה שֶׁל זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, וַאֲכַלְנוּהָ בַּפֶּסַח, וְאָכַלְנוּ וְלָדָהּ שְׁלָמִים בֶּחָג.

a13.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? אֲמַר קְרָא ״וְאִם זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים קׇרְבָּנוֹ לַה׳״, וְאֵם — וְלֹא וָלָד.

a14.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, ״אִם עַל תּוֹדָה יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ״, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאֵם וְלֹא וָלָד? וְכִי תֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָתַנְיָא: וְלָדָהּ, וּתְמוּרָתָהּ, וְחִילּוּפֶיהָ — מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִם עַל תּוֹדָה״ — מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.

a15.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יְגַדֵּל מֵהֶם עֲדָרִים עֲדָרִים.

a16.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ כּוּ׳.

a17.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הֵיכִי תָּנֵי? ״לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרְבוּ, אֶלָּא יִקְרְבוּ״, אוֹ דִילְמָא: ״לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ שֶׁיִּקְרְבוּ, אֶלָּא לֹא יִקְרְבוּ״?

a18.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִסְתַּבְּרָא ״לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרְבוּ, אֶלָּא יִקְרְבוּ״. מַאי טַעְמָא? עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבָּנַן אֶלָּא בְּוָלָד, אֲבָל וְלַד וָלָד — אַקְרַאי בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.

a19.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: ״לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ שֶׁיִּקְרְבוּ, אֶלָּא לֹא יִקְרְבוּ״. מַאי טַעְמָא? עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אֶלָּא בְּוָלָד, אֲבָל וְלַד וָלָד — מִתּוֹךְ (מַעֲשֶׂיהָ) [מַעֲשָׂיו] נִיכֶּרֶת מַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ דִּלְגַדֵּל קָא בָעֵי לֵיהּ.

b1.he: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְסַיּוֹעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: ״אִם כֶּשֶׂב הוּא מַקְרִיב״ — וָלָד רִאשׁוֹן קָרֵב, וָלָד שֵׁנִי אֵינוֹ קָרֵב.

b2.he: הוּא — קָרֵב, וְאֵין וְלַד כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים קָרֵב.

b3.he: וָלָד דְּמַאי? אִי דְּעוֹלָה וְאָשָׁם — זְכָרִים הֵם, וְלָא בְּנֵי וָלָד הֵם. אִי דְּחַטָּאת — הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ דִּלְמִיתָה אָזְלָא.

b4.he: אָמַר רָבִינָא: לְאֵיתוֹיֵי וְלַד הַמְעוּשֶּׂרֶת, וְלַד הַמְעוּשֶּׂרֶת לְמָה לִי קְרָא? ״עֲבָרָה״ ״עֲבָרָה״ מִבְּכוֹר קָא גָמַר לַהּ!

b5.he: אִצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אֲמִינָא: אֵין דָּנִין אֶפְשָׁר מִשֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b6.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי פַּפְּיָיס כּוּ׳.

b7.he: וּלְרָבָא דְּאָמַר: קָדָשִׁים, כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבַר עֲלֵיהֶם רֶגֶל אֶחָד, כָּל יוֹם וָיוֹם עוֹבֵר עֲלֵיהֶם בְּ״בַל תְּאַחֵר״, מֵעֲצֶרֶת בָּעֵי מֵיכְלֵיהּ! אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה חוֹלֶה בַּעֲצֶרֶת.

b8.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי ״חַג״ נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי? — חַג שָׁבוּעוֹת. וְאִידַּךְ, כֹּל הֵיכִי דְּקָתָנֵי ״פֶּסַח״ תָּנֵי ״עֲצֶרֶת״.

b9.he: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אַסְהָדוּתֵיהּ? לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, דְּאָמַר ״וְלַד שְׁלָמִים לֹא יִקְרַב שְׁלָמִים״, קָמַסְהֵיד הוּא דְּקָרֵב.

b10.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְלַד תּוֹדָה וּתְמוּרָתָהּ, וְלָדָן וְלַד וְלָדָן עַד סוֹף כׇּל הַדּוֹרוֹת — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כְּתוֹדָה, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁאֵין טְעוּנִין לֶחֶם.

b11.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַהוּ אוֹמֵר ״יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ״?

b12.he: מַפְרִישׁ תּוֹדָה, וְאָבְדָה, וְהִפְרִישׁ אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ, וְנִמְצֵאת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וַהֲרֵי שְׁתֵּיהֶן עוֹמְדוֹת. מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵיזוֹ שֶׁיִּרְצֶה יַקְרִיב וְלַחְמָהּ עִמָּהּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תּוֹדָה יַקְרִיב״.

b13.he: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא שְׁנִיָּה טְעוּנָה לֶחֶם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ״ — אַחַת וְלֹא שְׁתַּיִם. מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת וְלָדוֹת תְּמוּרוֹת וַחֲלִיפוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וְאִם עַל תּוֹדָה״. יָכוֹל יְהוּ כּוּלָּן טְעוּנוֹת לֶחֶם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״עַל זֶבַח הַתּוֹדָה״ — תּוֹדָה טְעוּנָה לֶחֶם, וְלֹא וְלָדָהּ וּתְמוּרָתָהּ וַחֲלִיפָתָהּ טְעוּנָה לֶחֶם.

b14.he: מַתְנִי׳ תְּמוּרַת עוֹלָה, וְלַד תְּמוּרָה, וְלַד וְלַד וְלָדָהּ עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כְּעוֹלָה, וּטְעוּנִין הֶפְשֵׁט וְנִיתּוּחַ וְכָלִיל לָאִשִּׁים. הַמַּפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְעוֹלָה וְיָלְדָה זָכָר — יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב וְיִמָּכֵר, וְיָבִיא בְּדָמָיו עוֹלָה. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הוּא עַצְמוֹ יִקְרַב עוֹלָה.

b15.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא פְּלִיגִי, וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא דִּפְלִיגִי?

b16.he: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה: בְּמַחְלוֹקֶת שְׁנוּיָה, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא. וְרָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, עַד כָּאן לָא פְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֶלָּא גַּבֵּי מַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְעוֹלָה, דְּאִימֵּיהּ לָא קְרֵיבָה, אֲבָל תְּמוּרָה דְּאִימֵּיהּ נָמֵי קְרֵיבָה — אֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן מוֹדוּ.

b17.he: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר יִקְרַב עוֹלָה הוּא עַצְמוֹ? וּרְמִינְהוּ: תְּמוּרַת אָשָׁם, וְלַד תְּמוּרָה, וְלָדָן, וְלַד וְלָדָן עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם — יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ, וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיִפְּלוּ דְּמֵיהֶן לִנְדָבָה.

b18.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יָמוּתוּ. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: יָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶן עוֹלָה. בַּדָּמִים — אִין, הוּא עַצְמוֹ — לָא.

b19.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ, לְדִידִי סְבִירָא לִי דַּאֲפִילּוּ וָלָד נָמֵי קָרֵב עוֹלָה, לְדִידְכוּ דְּאָמְרִיתוּ רוֹעֶה — אוֹדוֹ לִי מִיהַת דְּמוֹתָרוֹת לְנִדְבַת יָחִיד אָזְלִי, וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ: מוֹתָרוֹת לְנִדְבַת צִיבּוּר אָזְלִי.

b20.he: רָבָא אָמַר: עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הוּא עַצְמוֹ יִקְרַב עוֹלָה, אֶלָּא בְּמַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְעוֹלָה, דְּאִיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ,

messages.text: Continued from 17b: in Rabbi Yishmael’s baraita, “Only your holy things” excludes some offspring and substitutes from the altar, and the Gemara is asking which. Not a burnt offering’s, which is male and cannot give birth, nor a sin offering’s, which tradition says is left to die.

And if it is referring to the substitute of a guilt offering, it is learned as a tradition that this offering goes out to graze, as in any case where a sin offering is left to die, in the parallel case involving a guilt offering, the animal is left to graze until it develops a blemish, after which it is redeemed and the money is used to purchase a burnt offering. Therefore, there is no need for a verse to exclude the substitute of a guilt offering.

notes.he: וולד דאשם גופיה לא מצי אמרת דאשם גופיה זכר הוא ולא מוליד:
notes.en: If [it refers to] the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering: you cannot say the offspring of the guilt offering itself, since the guilt offering itself is a male and does not give birth.

messages.text: Actually, the baraita is referring to the offspring and substitute of a sin offering, and a verse is required to exclude them, despite the halakha that was learned as a tradition in their regard, for this halakha was learned only with regard to letting the animal die, and the verse serves to exclude them from being sacrificed on the altar.
But this, the halakha of sacrificing the animal upon the altar, depends on that, the halakha of letting it die. Since it goes to its death, it is clearly self-evident that it is not sacrificed.
messages.quote: the verse serves to exclude them from being sacrificed

notes.he: תיובתא הוא דקא מותיב:
notes.en: But this depends on that: it is a refutation that he raises.

messages.text: Rather, the halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai is referring to a sin offering, and the verse serves to exclude the case of a substitute of a guilt offering.

But this halakha with regard to the substitute of a guilt offering was also learned by the Sages as a tradition transmitted to Moses from Sinai, as they said that in any case where a sin offering is left to die, in the parallel case involving a guilt offering, the animal is left to graze.
messages.quote: to exclude the case of a substitute of a guilt offering

messages.text: Rather, the verse is necessary to teach an additional halakha, that if one transgressed and sacrificed the offspring of a sin offering or a guilt offering, or the substitute of a sin offering or a guilt offering, he stands in violation of a prohibition inferred from a positive mitzva. Since the verse teaches that only the offspring of a burnt offering or a peace offering may be offered, it may be inferred that the offspring of a guilt offering or a sin offering may not be offered, and the violation of a prohibition stemming from a command formulated as a positive mitzva is considered the violation of a positive mitzva.

notes.he: בין בחטאת ואשם קאי בעשה דמשמע רק קדשיך אלו תמורת עולה ושלמים וולדן ותמורתן דכתיב בתריה ועשית עולותיך וגו' ולא שאר קדשים כגון חטאת ואשם ולאו הבא מכלל עשה עשה:
notes.en: He stands in violation of a positive mitzva: with a sin offering and with a guilt offering alike he stands in violation of a positive mitzva, since “Only your holy things” implies: these are the substitutes of a burnt offering and a peace offering, and their offspring and their substitutes, as it is written after it, “And you shall offer your burnt offerings” etc., and not other sacrificial animals, such as a sin offering and a guilt offering. And a prohibition that comes by implication from a positive mitzva has the status of a positive mitzva.

notes.he: ודקאמרת (דלא) [והא] גמירי דמתה. כי גמיר הילכתא למיתה וקרא רק למעוטי מהקרבה. אלא הלכה לולד חטאת וקרא רק מיבעי דאם עבר ואקרביה לתמורת אשם ולולדה [אשם] (חטאת) קאי עליה בעשה. ואי זה עשה דהאי רק משמע דהני אין ולא בשאר קדשים היינו לאו הבא מכלל עשה [ולאו הבא מכלל עשה עשה:
notes.en: Actually, it refers to the offspring of a sin offering. And as for what you said, [but] it is learned that it dies: the halakha was learned for its death, and the verse “only” is to exclude it from being sacrificed. Rather, the halakha is for the offspring of a sin offering, and the verse “only” is needed [to teach] that if he transgressed and sacrificed the substitute of a guilt offering or its offspring, he stands in violation of a positive mitzva. And what positive mitzva is this? This “only” implies: these, yes, but not other sacrificial animals; that is a prohibition that comes by implication from a positive mitzva, [and a prohibition that comes by implication from a positive mitzva has the status of a positive mitzva.]

messages.text: The word “only” is unnecessary to exclude the offspring and substitutes of other sacrificial animals from being sacrificed upon the altar, as the verse that discusses guilt offerings: “It is a guilt offering” (Leviticus 5:19), teaches that only it, the guilt offering itself, is sacrificed, but its substitute is not offered.
messages.lead: § The baraita stated that in contrast to Rabbi Yishmael,

verse.en: It is a reparation offering; they have incurred guilt before GOD.

messages.text: Why do I need a verse to teach this? Didn’t the Sages learn this halakha, that the substitute of a guilt offering is left to graze, as a tradition transmitted to Moses from Sinai, since they said that in any case where a sin offering is left to die, in the parallel case involving a guilt offering, the animal is not sacrificed but rather left to graze?
messages.quote: it, the guilt offering itself, is sacrificed, but its substitute is not offered

notes.he: דכל שבחטאת מתה באשם רועה ותמורת חטאת מתה באשם רועה וכשיסתאב יפלו דמיו לנדבת צבור דהיינו עולה:
notes.en: But this halakha was learned as a tradition: that in any case where a sin offering is left to die, with a guilt offering it grazes; the substitute of a sin offering dies, so that of a guilt offering grazes, and when it becomes blemished its money goes to communal gift offerings, that is, a burnt offering.

notes.dh: ל"ל קרא והא הילכתא גמירי לה
notes.he: וא"ת לימא כדלעיל קרא מיבעי ליה דיעבד ומקריב קאי עלה בעשה וי"ל דהא לא משמע ליה עשה כ"כ כמו רק:
notes.en: Why do I need a verse; but this halakha was learned as a tradition: And if you will say: let him answer as above, that the verse is needed for where he transgressed and sacrificed, that he stands in violation of a positive mitzva. One can say: [“it is”] does not imply a positive mitzva as strongly as “only” does.

messages.text: Yes, it is indeed so, that the verse is unnecessary for that purpose. Rather, why do I need the verse? It is necessary to teach the halakha that Rav Huna stated,
messages.quote: Why do I need a verse to teach this?

messages.text: With regard to a guilt offering that was consigned to grazing, i.e., it had been ruled that the animal may not be sacrificed as a guilt offering, it must be left to graze until it develops a blemish, at which point it is sold and the proceeds used for voluntary burnt offerings. An example of this is where the owner had already fulfilled his obligation with the sacrifice of a different animal. If the owner nevertheless transgressed and slaughtered it before it developed a blemish as an unspecified offering, it is valid and sacrificed for the sake of a burnt offering.

notes.he: אם השלים לרועה וקדם ושחטו סתם עד שלא נסתאב כשר לעולה דהא סתמיה לשם עולה קאי לדמים:
notes.en: A guilt offering that was consigned to grazing: if [the court] handed it over to the shepherd, and he went ahead and slaughtered it unspecified before it became blemished, it is valid as a burnt offering, since when unspecified it stands for the sake of a burnt offering with regard to its value.

notes.dh: דאמר רב הונא אמר רב] אשם שניתק לרעיה
notes.he: כגון שהפריש אשם להתכפר בו ונאבד והפריש אשם אחר ונתכפרו בעליו (באחר) ואח"כ נמצא זה ואמר הגזבר שיצא לרעיה ואח"כ שחטו סתם כשר [לשום] עולה (ומנלן דכשר לעולה) [מ"ט כשר לשום עולה] דאשם הוי זכר וקדשי קדשים ועולה נמי זכר וקדשי קדשים:
notes.en: [As Rav Huna said that Rav said:] A guilt offering that was consigned to grazing: for example, one separated a guilt offering to atone with it, and it was lost, and he separated another guilt offering and its owner achieved atonement, and afterward this one was found, and the treasurer said that it goes out to graze, and afterward one slaughtered it unspecified: it is valid [for the sake of] a burnt offering. [What is the reason it is valid for the sake of a burnt offering?] Because a guilt offering is a male and an offering of the most sacred order, and a burnt offering too is a male and of the most sacred order. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads “Rav Huna said that Rav said”; the daf has Rav Huna alone.]

messages.text: If the animal was consigned to grazing, yes, it is valid as a burnt offering, but if it was not consigned to grazing, no, it is disqualified as a burnt offering.
messages.quote: a guilt offering that was consigned to grazing

notes.he: ואע"פ שכיפרו בעליו הואיל ועדיין לא ניתק דינו לרעייה ושחטו סתם פסול לגמרי:
notes.en: Not consigned, no: and even though its owner has achieved atonement [with another animal], since it has not yet been consigned by ruling to grazing, if he slaughtered it unspecified it is entirely disqualified.

notes.he: כלומר אם מאחר שניתק מדין אשם לרעיה שחטו סתם כשר לשם עולה דלאו שם אשם עליה. אבל אם לא ניתק ושחטו לשום עולה פסול הוא (אלמא) [דאשם] פסול הוי:
notes.en: Consigned, yes; not consigned, no: that is, if, after it was consigned from the law of a guilt offering to grazing, he slaughtered it unspecified, it is valid for the sake of a burnt offering, since the name of a guilt offering is no longer on it. But if it was not consigned and he slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt offering, it is disqualified, [since it is] a disqualified guilt offering.

messages.text: What is the reason? It is that the verse states with regard to a guilt offering: “It is a guilt offering,” meaning that it shall remain in its present state of a guilt offering.

notes.dh: מ"ט דאמר קרא אשם הוא בהווייתו יהא
notes.he: ועדיין אשם הוא ולא חזי לאקרוביה לאשם הילכך פסול:
notes.en: What is the reason? Because the verse states “It is”: it shall remain in its present state. It is still a guilt offering, and it is not fit to be sacrificed as a guilt offering; therefore it is disqualified.

notes.dh: ניתק אין לא ניתק לא מאי טעמא דאמר קרא הוא בהווייתו יהא
notes.he: ה"ג רש"י וקשה דהכא חזינן דבעי' ניתק מקרא ובפסחים פרק אלו עוברין (דף עג. ושם) איכא דבעי ניתוק משום גזירה (לפני כפרה אטו אחר כפרה) דהכי איתא אמר רב הונא אמר רב אשם שניתק לרעיה ושחטו סתם כשר לעולה אלמא לא בעי עקירה אי הכי מאי איריא ניתק אפילו כי לא ניתק נמי ומשני גזירה (לפני כפרה אטו לאחר כפרה) וע"ק דהכא אמר דלשם עולה כשר הא אמר בכולי הש"ס דהלכה למשה מסיני כל שבחטאת מתה באשם רועה לכן נראה [לר"ת] דהלכה למשה מסיני נגמרה באשם דקריבה עולה והכא ל"ג ניתק אין לא ניתק לא אלא גרסינן אשם שניתק לרעיה ושחטו סתמא כשר לעולה דאמר קרא הוא בהווייתו יהא פירוש בהווייתו שהוא עתיד להיות דהיינו עולה ובאותה הוויה יהא מעתה ומש"ה אפילו סתם כשר לעולה דלא בעי עקירה ומיהו איצטריך ההלכה למשה מסיני דאי לאו הכי לא הוה ידעינן מה הויה אית בה וללשון דאמר [בפסחים] באלו דברים (דף עג.) ושחטו לשם עולה כשר פירוש משמע אבל סתמא לא יהא כשר דבעי עקירה מ"ט דאמר קרא הוא בהווייתו יהא פירוש בהווייתו שהיה עתה יהא דיעקרנו לעולה ומיהו אצטריך ההלכה למשה מסיני דאי לאו הכי לא ה"א שיהא כשר לעולה אפילו ע"י עקירה:
notes.en: In brief: Rashi’s text reads: “Consigned, yes; not consigned, no. What is the reason? ‘It is’: it shall remain in its present state.” Tosafot finds this difficult on two counts. First, here consigning is required by a verse, while in Pesaḥim, in the chapter Elu Overin (73a), consigning is required only as a decree: Rav Huna said that Rav said, a guilt offering consigned to grazing and slaughtered unspecified is valid as a burnt offering, so no uprooting [of its name] is needed; then why specify consigned, when even not consigned it should be valid? And the answer there is: a decree [before atonement, on account of after atonement]. Second, here it says the animal is valid as a burnt offering, while throughout the Talmud the halakha to Moses from Sinai is that wherever a sin offering dies, a guilt offering grazes. Therefore Rabbeinu Tam holds that the halakha to Moses from Sinai concluded that with a guilt offering it is offered as a burnt offering, and here one does not read “consigned, yes; not consigned, no.” Rather the text reads: a guilt offering consigned to grazing and slaughtered unspecified is valid as a burnt offering, since the verse says “it is”: it shall remain in its being, meaning in what it is destined to be, a burnt offering, and from now on it is in that state; therefore even unspecified it is valid as a burnt offering and needs no uprooting. The halakha from Sinai was still needed, since without it we would not know what state it has. And according to the version in Pesaḥim (73a), “and he slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt offering, it is valid,” which implies that unspecified it is not valid because uprooting is needed, the reason is “it is”: it shall remain in its present state until he uproots it to a burnt offering; and the halakha from Sinai was still needed, since without it we would not have said that it is valid as a burnt offering even by uprooting. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.dh: מ"ט דאמר קרא הוא בהווייתו יהא
notes.he: כלומר כיון דלא ניתק אע"פ ששינה שמו ושחטו לשום עולה בהווייתו יהא ואשם פסול הוא ולא קרב. אבל שאר זבחים דלא כתב בהו הוא (קרא) בין ניתק ובין לא ניתק כי שחטו לשם זבח אחד כשרים אלא שלא עלו לבעלים [לשום חובה] כדתנן כל הזבחים ששחטו שלא לשמן כו':
notes.en: What is the reason? Because the verse states “It is”: it shall remain in its present state. That is, since it was not consigned, even though he changed its name and slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt offering, it remains in its present state, and it is a disqualified guilt offering and is not sacrificed. But other offerings, about which “it is” is not written, whether consigned or not consigned, when one slaughtered them for the sake of another offering they are valid, except that they do not count for the owner [toward his obligation], as we learned: All offerings that were slaughtered not for their own sake, etc. [Zevaḥim 2a].

messages.text: § The Gemara previously (17b) cited two baraitot that stated that the offspring of a peace offering has the status of a peace offering. According to one, this is derived from the phrase in the verse in Leviticus “if male if female,” while according to the other it is derived from the phrase in the verse in Deuteronomy “You shall take and go.”

And according to this tanna of the second baraita, who derives this halakha from these verses: “You shall take and go,” and: “And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood,” let him derive it from the words “male” and “female.”
He requires that verse to teach the halakha of the offspring of a blemished animal and to teach the halakha of the substitute of a blemished animal.

And let him derive all of the halakhot, that of the offspring and the substitute of an unblemished peace offering as well as that of the offspring and the substitute of a blemished offering, from this verse: “If male if female,” in the same manner that the tanna of the first baraita derived them from that verse.
messages.quote: offspring of a blemished animal

notes.he: דהא כולהו דרשינן להו לעיל מיניה:
notes.en: And let him derive all of them from it: since we expounded all of them from it above.

notes.he: כולהו בין בולד תמימין בין בעלי מומין בין תמורת תמימין בין תמורת בעלי מומין:
notes.en: And let him derive all of them: whether for the offspring of unblemished animals or of blemished animals, whether for the substitute of unblemished animals or of blemished animals.

messages.text: He does not learn anything from the word “if,” which is a common term and is not considered superfluous.

notes.he: מזכר (ומאם) ומנקבה ומאם אם לא משמע ליה למידרש מיניה כלום הילכך מפיק לזכר ונקבה לולד בעלי מומין ולתמורת בעלי מומין ורק קדשיך לולדי תמימים ותמורת תמימ' [תיפוק לי] מן תשא ובאת ועשית עולותיך דמהתם ילפינן דקרבי:
notes.en: From “male” and from “female”: “if” he does not consider to imply anything to expound from it. Therefore he takes “male” and “female” for the offspring of blemished animals and for the substitute of blemished animals, and “only your holy things” for the offspring of unblemished animals and the substitute of unblemished animals, [deriving it] from “you shall take and go” and “you shall offer your burnt offerings,” since from there we derive that they are sacrificed.

messages.text: And according to this tanna of the first baraita, who derives all of the halakhot from the words “if male if female,” what does he do with the phrase in the verse “You shall take and go”?

That verse is necessary to teach that one must bring his offerings to the Temple when he ascends to Jerusalem for the Festival even if he must take them from their place of grazing, and he should not delay bringing them until the following Festival.

notes.he: האי תשא ובאת לאו לולדות ותמורות אתא אלא לקדשים עצמן דקא מזהר לו לאיתויי הייא אפילו הן במרעה באפר והגיע זמן הרגל לעלות לא יאמר איני טורח אחריהן לבקשן באגם ולהוליכן אבל אמתין לי עד פעם אחרת:
notes.en: “You shall take and go”: even from their grazing. This “you shall take and go” does not come for offspring and substitutes but for the sacrificial animals themselves, warning him to bring them even if they are at pasture in the meadow and the time of the Festival has come to go up. He should not say: I will not trouble myself to seek them in the marsh and bring them, but I will wait until another time.

notes.he: פרש"י אפילו הן במרעה באפר והגיע זמן הרגל לא יאמר איני טורח אחריהם לבקשם באגם ולהוליכם אבל אמתין לי עד פעם אחרת לישנא אחרינא אפילו ממורגייהו כלומר אפילו הן דשין את התבואה במוריגים עכ"ל ולא נהירא שהרי אסור היה בעבודה ור"י מפרש מדארגייהו אפילו הן דלות בשר דסד"א כיון שהם תשושי כח אינו צריך להעלותם הואיל ואינו תחילת הקדש כגון ולדות ותמורות כי שמטו הבקר (שמואל ב ו) מתרגמינן ארי איתמריגו תורתא וה"ר יצחק בר שניאור פירש ממרעייהו אפילו ממקום שמותר לרעותה ולגדלה דהיינו בחו"ל דאין מגדלין בהמה בא"י וזו היא הדרשה דאיתא בספרי רק קדשיך אשר יהיו לך מכאן שמביאין קדשים מחו"ל יכול אף בכור ומעשר כן ת"ל רק ומה ראית לרבות את אלו ולהוציא את אלו אחר שריבה הכתוב ומיעט מרבה אני את אלו שאין להן פרנסה במקומן כלומר אינן נאכלין במומן בחו"ל ומוציא אני את אלו שיש להן פרנסה במקומן כלומר שנאכלין במומן בחו"ל:
notes.en: Even from their grazing [mimiraihu]: Rashi explained: even if they are at pasture in the meadow and the time of the Festival has come, he should not say, I will not trouble myself to seek them in the marsh and bring them, but I will wait until another time. Another version: even from their threshing-boards, meaning, even if they are threshing grain with threshing-boards. [End of his words.] This is not clear, since it was forbidden to work [a consecrated animal]. And the Ri explains “from their weakness” [mide’argaihu]: even if they are lean of flesh. For one might have thought that since they are weak he need not bring them up, since they are not the original consecration, such as offspring and substitutes; as for “for the oxen stumbled” (II Samuel 6:6), the Targum renders “for the oxen were weakened [itmerigu].” And Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Shneur explained “from their grazing”: even from a place where it is permitted to graze and raise it, that is, outside the Land, since one does not raise livestock in the Land of Israel. And this is the exposition in the Sifrei: “Only your holy things that you have”: from here, that one brings sacrificial animals from outside the Land. One might think the same is true of a firstborn and tithe; the verse states “only.” What did you see to include these and exclude those? After the verse included and excluded, I include these, which have no sustenance in their place, that is, they are not eaten in their blemished state outside the Land, and I exclude those, which have sustenance in their place, that is, they are eaten in their blemished state outside the Land.

notes.he: ל"א אפילו מן מרעיהו שאם רועין באגם במקום רחוק חייב לילך לשם ולהביאן:
notes.en: Another version: even from their grazing: if they are pasturing in the marsh in a distant place, he is obligated to go there and bring them.

messages.text: The verse is necessary to teach that one must bring the animals he intends to consecrate even if he must take them from their place of threshing, i.e., even if they are currently being used to thresh, rather than delay bringing the animals to Jerusalem until a later stage.

notes.he: אפילו הן דשין את התבואה במוריגים דאמרינן במנחות בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כב.) מאי מוריגי עיזי דקורקסא דדיישי דישתא נסר גדול מנוקב ויתידות קבועות בו ונותנין אותן על התבואה ומרהיטים עליו את הבהמות ואתא קרא למימר דאם דשה הבהמה שאתה רוצה להקדיש ודרכך מוכן לעלות לרגל לא תאמר הואיל ודשה אמתין עד זמן אחר אלא קחנה ולך לך:
notes.en: Another version: even from their threshing-boards [morigim]: even if they are threshing grain with threshing-boards, as we say in Menaḥot, in the chapter HaKometz Rabba (Menaḥot 22a): What are morigim? “Izei dekurkesa” with which they thresh. [That is,] a large perforated board with pegs set in it; they lay it on the grain and drive the animals over it. And the verse comes to say: if the animal you wish to consecrate is threshing, and you are about to go up for the Festival, do not say, since it is threshing I will wait until another time; rather, take it and go.

notes.dh: אמר לך תשא ובאת להכי אתא
notes.he: דכיון דהגיע הרגל אי אתה רשאי לעכב מלהביא קדשיך ונדריך מיד אלא תיטול אותם אפילו מן (מורגיהו) [ממורגייהו] כלומר שאפילו אם נכנסו מעצמן על הגורן ועל התבואה ועל המוריגים ודשין תקח אותם משם ותביאם לבית הבחירה. אבל במתכוין אסור לדוש בהן דהיינו עבודה:
notes.en: He would say to you: “You shall take and go” comes for this: once the Festival has arrived, you are not permitted to hold back from bringing your sacrificial animals and your vows immediately; rather, take them even from their threshing-boards [morigim]. That is, even if they went of their own accord onto the threshing floor, onto the grain and onto the threshing-boards, and are threshing, take them from there and bring them to the Temple. But intentionally it is forbidden to thresh with them, since that is labor. [Rabbeinu Gershom gives the “threshing” reading as the main answer and “grazing” as the other version, the reverse of the printed Gemara.]

messages.text: Mishna
Although the previous mishna (17b) stated plainly that the offspring of a peace offering is itself sacrificed as a peace offering, its status is actually subject to a dispute between the tanna’im.
The offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed on the altar as a peace offering; rather it is sequestered and left to die.

notes.he: אלא כונסו לכיפה ומת ומדרבנן ומשום גזירה דלקמן דודאי מסיני לא גמירי אלא ה' חטאות מתות:
notes.en: MISHNA: It is not sacrificed as a peace offering: rather, it is placed in a vaulted chamber and dies. And this is by rabbinic law, because of the decree [explained] below, since certainly from Sinai only the five sin offerings that are left to die were learned.

notes.dh: רבי אליעזר אומר ולד שלמים לא יקרב
notes.he: ומדרבנן הוא כדמפרש בגמ' שמא יגדל ממנו עדרים עדרים:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: The offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed: and this is by rabbinic law, as the Gemara explains: lest he raise herds upon herds from it.

messages.text: It is sacrificed as a peace offering.

notes.he: צ"ע חכמים היינו ת"ק:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: It is sacrificed: this requires further study: the Rabbis are [the same as] the first tanna [of the previous mishna].

messages.text: Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis do not disagree with regard to the status of the offspring of the offspring of a peace offering or with regard to the status of the offspring of the offspring of the substitute of a peace offering. In those cases, they all agree that the animal is not sacrificed on the altar as a peace offering.

notes.dh: לא נחלקו על ולד ולד שלמים ועל ולד ולד תמורה
notes.he: בגמ' מפרש לה:
notes.en: They do not disagree about the offspring of the offspring of a peace offering and about the offspring of the offspring of a substitute: the Gemara explains it.

messages.text: With regard to what case do they disagree? They disagree about the case of the offspring of a peace offering itself. Rabbi Eliezer says: It is not sacrificed as a peace offering, whereas the Rabbis say: It is sacrificed.
Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Pappeyas testified about the offspring of a peace offering that it is sacrificed as a peace offering.
I testify that we ourselves had a cow that was a peace offering, and we ate it on Passover, and we ate its offspring as a peace offering on a different Festival.
Gemara

What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer, that the offspring of a peace offering does not have the status of a peace offering? It is that the verse states with regard to a peace offering: “And if his offering be a sacrifice of peace offerings for the Lord” (Leviticus 3:1). The term “and if [ve’im],” can be read as: And a mother [ve’em], which teaches that the mother may be offered as a peace offering, but not the offspring.
messages.quote: The offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed

verse.he: וְאִם־זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים קׇרְבָּנוֹ אִם מִן־הַבָּקָר הוּא מַקְרִיב אִם־זָכָר אִם־נְקֵבָה תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en:
If your offering is a sacrifice of well-being uncertain.—
If you offer of the herd, whether a male or a female, you shall bring before GOD one without blemish.

notes.he: ודריש להאי אם כמו אם בצירי:
notes.en: GEMARA: “And if [ve’im] a sacrifice of peace offerings”: he expounds this “im” as if it were “em” [mother], with a tzere.

notes.he: משמע אם ולא ולד. וחילופה. היינו שהפריש תמורה ואבדה והפריש אחרת תחתיה:
notes.en: [“If”: a mother and not offspring. “If” implies a mother [em] and not an offspring. And its replacement: that is, he separated a substitute and it was lost, and he separated another in its place.

messages.text: @Rabbi Ami If that is so, then with regard to the verse: “If [im] he offer it for a thanksgiving” (Leviticus 7:12), so too one should interpret it to mean that one may sacrifice the mother [em] but not the offspring as a thanks offering.
messages.quote: And a mother [ve’em] … but not the offspring

verse.he: אִם עַל־תּוֹדָה יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ וְהִקְרִיב ׀ עַל־זֶבַח הַתּוֹדָה חַלּוֹת מַצּוֹת בְּלוּלֹת בַּשֶּׁמֶן וּרְקִיקֵי מַצּוֹת מְשֻׁחִים בַּשָּׁמֶן וְסֹלֶת מֻרְבֶּכֶת חַלֹּת בְּלוּלֹת בַּשָּׁמֶן׃
verse.en: One who offers it for thanksgiving shall offer, together with the sacrifice of thanksgiving, unleavened cakes with oil mixed in—unleavened wafers spread with oil—and cakes of choice flour with oil mixed in, well soaked.

messages.text: And if you would say that Rabbi Eliezer indeed holds that the offspring of a thanks offering is not sacrificed as a thanks offering, isn’t it taught in a baraita:

With regard to the offspring of a thanks offering and its substitute and its replacement, if the original animal was lost and then found again, rendering both animals suitable for an offering: From where is it derived that all these are sacrificed as thanks offerings? The verse states: “If for a thanksgiving,” which indicates that they may be offered as a thanks offering in any case.

notes.he: כגון אבדה והפריש אחרת תחתיה ונמצאת הראשונה והרי שתיהן עומדות:
notes.en: And its replacement: for example, it was lost, and he separated another in its place, and the first was found, and now both of them stand [before him].

notes.he: האי אם מרבה לכולהו דקרב להו ולא פליג ר"א:
notes.en: The verse states “If for a thanksgiving”: this “if” includes all of them, that they are sacrificed, and Rabbi Eliezer does not disagree.

notes.he: היינו אבדה והפריש אחרת תחתיה ונמצאת הראשונה והרי שתיהן עומדות:
notes.en: And its replacement: that is, it was lost, and he separated another in its place, and the first was found, and now both of them stand [before him].

messages.text: This is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer, that the offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed as a peace offering: It is a rabbinic decree that it may not be sacrificed, lest the owner delay sacrificing the peace offerings that he is obligated to bring so that he may raise entire herds from them in order to sell the animals to people who need peace offerings.
messages.lead: Rather, Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

notes.he: אי אמרת ולד שלמים יש לו תקנה אתי לשהוייה לאם עד שתלד ויגדל עדרים מן הולדות ואתו בהו לידי גיזה ועבודה. ובתודה ה"ט דלא גזר משום דתודה לא שכיחא כשלמים:
notes.en: A decree: if you say that the offspring of a peace offering has a remedy, he will come to keep the mother back until it gives birth, and raise herds from the offspring, and come through them to shearing and labor [with consecrated animals]. And with a thanks offering, the reason he did not decree is that a thanks offering is not as common as a peace offering.

notes.he: שאם אתה אומר ולד שלמים יקרב]:
notes.en: A decree: that if you say the offspring of a peace offering is sacrificed,]

notes.he: ישהא אותם עד שיגדל מהם הרבה ושמא יבא (מהן) לידי תקלה שיאכל מהן כסבור של חולין הן:
notes.en: Lest he raise herds upon herds from them: he will keep them back until he raises many from them, and perhaps he will come to a mishap, eating of them in the belief that they are non-sacred.

messages.text: Rabbi Shimon said: Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis do not disgree with regard to the status of the offspring of the offspring of a peace offering, or with regard to the status of the offspring of the offspring of the substitute of a peace offering. In those cases, they all agree that the animal is not sacrificed on the altar as a peace offering. With regard to what case do they disagree? They disagree only about the offspring of a peace offering itself.
messages.quote: do not disagree with regard to the status of the offspring of the offspring of a peace offering

notes.dh: אמר ר"א לא נחלקו על ולד [ולד] שלמים ועל ולד [ולד] תמורה שלא יקרב
notes.he: בהא פליגי אמוראי בגמ' רבה אמר מסתברא שלא נחלקו שלא יקרבו אלא יקרבו ורבי יהושע בן לוי אמר לא נחלקו שיקרבו אלא לא יקרבו ולפי דברי רבי יהושע בן לוי איכא ג' מחלוקות בדבר ת"ק דר"ש סבר אליבא דת"ק כולהו קרבי ולר"א כולהו לא קרבי ור"ש סבר דכ"ע אחר ולד ראשון דלא קרבי ולא פליגי אלא בולד ראשון ובגמ' מפרש טעמייהו:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon said: They do not disagree about the offspring [of the offspring] of a peace offering and about the offspring [of the offspring] of a substitute, that it is not sacrificed: the Amoraim in the Gemara disagree about this. Rabba said: It stands to reason that they do not disagree [such that one says] they are not sacrificed; rather, they are sacrificed. And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: They do not disagree [such that one says] they are sacrificed; rather, they are not sacrificed. And according to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi there are three opinions in the matter. The first tanna, [before] Rabbi Shimon, holds that according to the first tanna [the Rabbis] all of them are sacrificed and according to Rabbi Eliezer none of them is sacrificed; and Rabbi Shimon holds that all agree that after the first offspring they are not sacrificed, and they disagree only about the first offspring. And the Gemara explains their reasons.

notes.dh: לא נחלקו על ולד שלמים ולא על ולד תמורה
notes.he: ולד תמורה היינו כולד ולד שלמים ועל מה נחלקו על הולד עצמו [של שלמים]:
notes.en: They do not disagree about the offspring of a peace offering, nor about the offspring of a substitute: the offspring of a substitute is like the offspring of the offspring of a peace offering. And about what do they disagree? About the offspring itself [of a peace offering].

messages.text: How precisely is the mishna taught? Is it saying that Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis do not disagree whether the offspring of the offspring are sacrificed or they are not sacrificed, but rather they all agree, even Rabbi Eliezer, that they are sacrificed?
messages.lead: A dilemma was raised before the Sages:

notes.he: האי שלא יקרבו דקאמר ר"ש ריש מילתיה היא וה"ק לא נחלקו שיאמר ר"א לא יקרבו אלא ודאי יקרבו או סוף מילתיה היא וה"ק לא נחלקו דודאי לא יקרבו אפילו לרבנן מי מודה ר"א בהא דאישתכחן להון דרי אי לא (וולד וולד) אישתכחן להו דרי דאין אדם נזכר שמשלמים באו ואין לגזור שמא יראו אחרים שזה מקריבן וישהו את שלמיהן לצורך ולדות לגדל מהן עדרים:
notes.en: How is it taught? Is this “that it is not sacrificed,” which Rabbi Shimon says, the beginning of his statement, so that he is saying: they do not disagree such that Rabbi Eliezer would say it is not sacrificed; rather, certainly it is sacrificed? Or is it the end of his statement, so that he is saying: they do not disagree, since certainly it is not sacrificed, even according to the Rabbis? [The question is:] does Rabbi Eliezer concede in this case, where they are found to have generations, or not? [With the offspring of the offspring,] they are found to have generations, so a person does not remember that they came from a peace offering, and there is no need to decree lest others see that this one sacrifices them and delay their own peace offerings for the sake of the offspring, to raise herds from them.

notes.he: לא יחלקו חכמים על ולד ולד שיקרב אלא לא יקרב וסוף מילתא נקט היינו יקרב דאהכי לא פליגי:
notes.en: How is it taught? [That] the Sages do not disagree about the offspring of the offspring, [saying] that it is sacrificed; rather, it is not sacrificed. And he took the end of the statement, that is, “it is sacrificed,” since about this they do not disagree. [The wording here is unclear. Rabbeinu Gershom’s first option is the “not sacrificed” reading, which the printed Gemara gives second.]

messages.text: Or perhaps it is saying that they do not disagree whether the offspring of the offspring are sacrificed or they are not sacrificed, but rather they all agree, even the Sages, that they are not sacrificed.

notes.he: הכי קתני לא נחלק ר' אליעזר בולד ולד שלא יקרב אלא יקרב. כלומר (דאדיש) [דארישא] דמילתא (לא פליג) [פלגינן] דהיינו לא יקרב [אלא יקרב] דכי גזר ר' אליעזר דלא יקרב שמא יגדל מהן עדרים היינו אולד ראשון אבל ולד ולד יקרב (דסבר ר' אליעזר) [דכברי] אשכחן להון דרי והואיל והוא דור שני אין זוכרין שהוא ולד ולד שלמים וליכא למיחש שמא יגדל מהן עדרים [ואית דגרסי אבל בולד ולד לא גזר דאקראי בעלמא הוא משתכח ולד ולד ליכא למיחש:
notes.en: Or perhaps this is how it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer does not disagree about the offspring of the offspring, [saying] that it is not sacrificed; rather, it is sacrificed. That is, we divide at the beginning of the statement, “it is not sacrificed,” [rather it is sacrificed]. For when Rabbi Eliezer decreed that it is not sacrificed, lest he raise herds from them, that was about the first offspring; but the offspring of the offspring is sacrificed, since they are already found to have generations, and since it is a second generation, people do not remember that it is the offspring of the offspring of a peace offering, and there is no concern lest he raise herds from them. [And some read: but about the offspring of the offspring he did not decree, since it is found only by mere chance; about the offspring of the offspring there is no concern.

messages.text: It stands to reason that the mishna is saying that they do not disagree whether the offspring of the offspring are not sacrificed, but rather all agree that they are sacrificed. What is the reason? It is that Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with the Rabbis only with regard to the offspring, but with regard to the offspring of the offspring, Rabbi Eliezer does not render it prohibited to sacrifice them, as it is merely a chance, i.e., an uncommon occurrence, that one delays sacrificing an offering to the point that the offspring of its offspring have already been born.

notes.he: ולא שכיח לשהותו כל כך:
notes.en: It is merely a chance: it is not common to delay it so long.

messages.text: The correct reading of the mishna is: They do not disagree whether the offspring of the offspring are sacrificed, but rather all agree that they are not sacrificed. What is the reason? It is that the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer only with regard to the offspring, but with regard to the offspring of the offspring, from the result of his actions with regard to it, i.e., that he delayed sacrificing the original offering for such a long period of time, his intention is evident that he wants to raise herds from it. Therefore, the halakha is that the offspring of the offspring may not be sacrificed, in order to deter him from the outset from raising herds.

notes.he: משום דגלי דעתיה דמתוך מעשיו ששיירו עד שהיה לו] ולד ולד וניכרת מחשבתו דלגדל עדרים קא בעי ליה הילכך לא יקרב:
notes.en: Because he has revealed his mind: since from his actions, that he left it until he had] an offspring of an offspring, his intention is evident that he wants it to raise herds; therefore it is not sacrificed.

messages.caption: Rabbi Shimon’s report of the dispute over a peace offering’s offspring, as Rabba and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi each read it.

messages.text: The verse states: “If he sacrifices a lamb for his offering, then shall he present it before the Lord” (Leviticus 3:7). Two limitations are derived from this verse: The word “lamb” indicates that the first offspring, i.e., the offspring of the peace offering, is sacrificed, but the second offspring, i.e., the offspring of the offspring, is not sacrificed.
messages.lead: § Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches a baraita to support the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, that all agree that the offspring of the offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed:

verse.he: אִם־כֶּשֶׂב הוּא־מַקְרִיב אֶת־קׇרְבָּנוֹ וְהִקְרִיב אֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If you present a sheep as your offering, you shall bring it before GOD

notes.he: משמע ולד טלה:
notes.en: A lamb: implies the offspring of a lamb.

notes.he: תני רבי חייא לסיועי לר' יהושע בן לוי אם כשב הוא מקדיש ולד ראשון הוא קרב ולד שני אינו קרב - והיינו ע"כ כרבנן דאי לר"א ולד ראשון אינו קרב כלל והך דרשה אינה אלא אסמכתא בעלמא דהא ודאי הא דולד שני אינו קרב היינו מדרבנן שמא יגדל ממנו עדרים עדרים ובפסחים (דף צו:) מוקי לה להאי לדרשא אחרינא:
notes.en: Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches to support Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: “If he offers a lamb”: the first offspring is sacrificed, the second offspring is not sacrificed: and this is necessarily according to the Rabbis, since according to Rabbi Eliezer the first offspring is not sacrificed at all. And this exposition is merely a supporting allusion [asmakhta], since certainly the rule that the second offspring is not sacrificed is rabbinic, lest he raise herds upon herds from it. And in Pesaḥim (96b) this verse is applied to a different exposition.

notes.he: לא צריך למיכתב ואם (ואם כשב) יביא קרבנו והקריב אותה לפני ה' אלא הוא מקריב להכי אתא דהוא ולד ראשון קרב ולד ולד אין קרב:
notes.en: “If he offers a lamb”: [the verse] did not need to write “And if he brings a lamb as his offering, he shall present it before the Lord”; rather, “he offers” comes for this: that it, the first offspring, is sacrificed; the offspring of the offspring is not sacrificed.

messages.text: In addition, the word “he [hu]” is interpreted as referring to the offspring of the peace offering rather than the owner, as it is obvious from the context that the owner is sacrificing the animal and the word would be unnecessary if written only for that purpose. Therefore, it teaches that the offspring of a peace offering is sacrificed, but the offspring of all other sacrificial animals is not sacrificed. This indicates that even those Sages who rule that the offspring of a peace offering is sacrificed agree that the offspring of the offspring is not sacrificed.

notes.he: ולד שלמים דהא קרא בשלמים כתיב:
notes.en: “He” is sacrificed: the offspring of a peace offering, since the verse is written about peace offerings.

messages.text: The offspring of which type of offering is referred to here? If it is referring to that of a burnt offering or guilt offering, they are male and therefore not capable of giving birth to offspring. If it is referring to the offspring of a sin offering, the verse is unnecessary, as the Sages learned this halakha as a tradition that it is left to die and may not be offered.
messages.quote: but the offspring of all other sacrificial animals is not sacrificed

notes.he: קא ממעט דאמרת ואין ולד כל הקדשים קריבין:
notes.en: The offspring of which: is he excluding, when you said “and the offspring of all sacrificial animals is not sacrificed”?

notes.he: שאר קדשים איצטריך למעט אי דעולה ואשם כו':
notes.en: The offspring of which: of other sacrificial animals did [the verse] need to exclude? If of a burnt offering and a guilt offering, etc.

messages.text: The verse serves to include, in the limitation that the offspring of other sacrificial animals are not sacrificed, the offspring of an animal that was consecrated as animal tithe and then gave birth.
messages.quote: The offspring of which type of offering is referred to here?

notes.he: מעשר בהמה שיצאה נקבה בעשירי ואחר כך ילדה ולדה אינו קרב אלא ירעה ויאכל במומו לבעלים כדין מעשר שנאכל במומו לבעלים:
notes.en: The offspring of a tithe animal: an animal tithe that came out as the tenth and was a female, and afterward gave birth. Its offspring is not sacrificed; rather, it grazes and is eaten by its owners once blemished, like the law of the tithe, which is eaten by its owners once blemished.

notes.he: דלא קרב. מה בכור לא קרב ולד דידיה דלאו בר ולד הוא דבכור זכר הוי:
notes.en: [Ravina said: To include the offspring of a tithe animal, that it is not sacrificed. Just as with a firstborn its offspring is not sacrificed, since it is not capable of offspring, as a firstborn is a male.

messages.text: Why do I need a verse to include the offspring of the animal tithe? It is derived through a verbal analogy between the word passing [avara] mentioned with regard to animal tithe, and the word passing [avara] mentioned with regard to a firstborn animal, which is male and cannot give birth to offspring.
messages.quote: the offspring of an animal that was consecrated as animal tithe

notes.he: ובבכור לא קרב ולד דידיה דהא ליכא ולד בבכור דהא זכר הוא:
notes.en: It is derived from the firstborn: and with a firstborn its offspring is not sacrificed, since a firstborn has no offspring, as it is a male.

messages.text: With regard to animal tithe the verse states: “And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatsoever passes [ya’avor] under the rod, the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord” (Leviticus 27:32),

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

messages.text: and with regard to a firstborn, the verse states: “And you shall set apart [veha’avarta] for the Lord all that opens the womb; every firstborn that is a male, which you have that comes of an animal, shall be the Lord’s” (Exodus 13:12).

verse.he: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כׇל־פֶּטֶר־רֶחֶם לַיהֹוָה וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר ׀ שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ הַזְּכָרִים לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: you shall set apart for GOD every first issue of the womb: every male firstling that your cattle drop shall be GOD’s.

messages.text: This verse is necessary, as it might enter your mind to say that one does not derive the possible from the impossible, as in this case, where one seeks to derive by way of analogy the halakha of the offspring of animal tithe from that of a firstborn, which is a male and therefore cannot give birth. Therefore, the verse teaches us that the offspring of animal tithe is not sacrificed on the altar as an offering.

notes.he: הוא למעט וולד מעשר דסד"א אין דנין אפשר מעשר דנוהג נמי בנקבה ואית להו ולד מבכור דאי אפשר דאין לו ולד אלא יקרב ולד מעשר קמ"ל הוא ולא ולד שאר קדשים:
notes.en: It is necessary: “he” [is needed] to exclude the offspring of tithe. For it might enter your mind to say: one does not derive the possible, the tithe, which applies to females too, and they have offspring, from the firstborn, where it is impossible, since it has no offspring; and so the offspring of tithe would be sacrificed. It teaches us: “he,” and not the offspring of other sacrificial animals.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Pappeyas testified about the offspring of a peace offering that it is sacrificed as a peace offering. Rabbi Pappeyas added the testimony that he had a cow that was eaten as a peace offering on Passover, and its offspring was eaten as a peace offering on a different Festival [beḥag].
messages.quote: we ate it on Passover, and we ate its offspring as a peace offering on a different Festival

messages.text: The William Davidson English here reads “Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Pappeyas testified”; the Aramaic of the daf reads Rabbi Yehoshua, as the mishna above does.

And according to the opinion of Rava, who said with regard to sacrificial animals that once one pilgrimage Festival has passed from when they were consecrated, and the owner has not yet brought them to the Temple, each day he transgresses with regard to them the prohibition of: You shall not delay, which is derived from the verse that states: “When you shall vow a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not delay to pay it” (Deuteronomy 23:22), already from Shavuot he must eat the offspring of the peace offering that was sacrificed on Passover. Why then did they wait until Sukkot?
messages.lead: Since the term ḥag generally refers to Sukkot:

verse.he: כִּי־תִדֹּר נֶדֶר לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תְאַחֵר לְשַׁלְּמוֹ כִּי־דָרֹשׁ יִדְרְשֶׁנּוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מֵעִמָּךְ וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא׃
verse.en: When you make a vow to the ETERNAL your God, do not put off fulfilling it, for the ETERNAL your God will require it of you, and you will have incurred guilt;

notes.he: ובאת שמה והבאתם שם דמשמע ברגל ראשון שתבא שמה הבא כל נדרים שעליך:
notes.en: Each day he transgresses a positive mitzva: “And there you shall come… and there you shall bring” (Deuteronomy 12:5–6), which implies: on the first Festival on which you come there, bring all the vows that are upon you. [Rashi’s text reads “transgresses a positive mitzva,” where the printed Gemara has “You shall not delay.”]

notes.he: דבשלמא בפסח לא אקרביה דאימור מחוסר זמן הוה דנולד בפסח ועבר הרגל קודם שימלאו לו ז' ימים:
notes.en: He must eat it from Shavuot: granted, on Passover they did not sacrifice it, since perhaps it was lacking in time: it was born on Passover, and the Festival passed before it was seven days old.

notes.he: אבל לא פריך מפסח בעי למיכליה דאפשר דמחוסר זמן היה:
notes.en: He must eat it from Shavuot: but he does not object that he must eat it from Passover, since it is possible that it was lacking in time.

messages.text: It is referring to a case where the owner was unable to sacrifice the offspring of the peace offering on Shavuot due to circumstances beyond his control, for example, if the animal was ill on Shavuot [ba’Atzeret].

notes.he: כגון שהיה הולד חולה בעצרת דלא הוי ראוי להקרבה]:
notes.en: For example, the offspring was ill on Shavuot, so that it was not fit to be sacrificed.]

messages.text: What is the meaning of the word ḥag that is taught in the mishna in the testimony of Rabbi Pappeyas? It is referring to the festival of Shavuot, not Sukkot.

notes.he: ואכלנו ולדה שלמים בחג בעצרת דחג הואי:
notes.en: What is the ḥag that is taught? “And we ate its offspring as a peace offering on the Festival [beḥag]”: on Shavuot, which is a festival.

messages.text: And the other amora, Rav Zevid, why didn’t he explain the mishna in this manner? Wherever the tanna teaches the word Pesaḥ in a mishna, and he wishes also to teach something about Shavuot, he uses the term atzeret rather than the word ḥag.
messages.quote: It is referring to the festival of Shavuot

notes.he: רב זביד אמר לך כל היכא דתני פסח ובעי לאדכורי מידי בעצרת תני עצרת ולא קרי ליה חג אבל אי הוה מדכר לפסח בלשון חג המצות הוה תני לעצרת בלשון חג:
notes.en: And the other: Rav Zevid would say to you: wherever he teaches Passover and wishes to mention something about Shavuot, he teaches “Atzeret” and does not call it “ḥag.” But had he mentioned Passover with the term “the festival [ḥag] of matzot,” he would have taught Shavuot with the term “ḥag.”

notes.he: ורב זביד אמר אי [האי] בעצרת קא מיירי בחג שבועות הא קרי ליה אלא כיון דאמר בחג סתם היינו סכות והאי דלא אקרבוה בעצרת משום דהוה חולה:
notes.en: And Rav Zevid said: if this were speaking of Shavuot, he would have called it “the festival of weeks”; but since he said “on the Festival” unspecified, that is Sukkot. And the reason they did not sacrifice it on Shavuot is that it was ill.

messages.text: If so, that the offspring of the peace offering was not sacrificed on Shavuot due to illness, as suggested by Rava, or that it was indeed sacrificed on Shavuot, as proposed by Rav Ashi, what is the purpose of the testimony of Rabbi Pappeyas? He certainly cannot be excluding the opinion shared by Rava, as might have been indicated by a straightforward reading of the mishna.

notes.he: דהאי חג שבועות הוא א"נ דהוה חולה:
notes.en: If so: that this ḥag is Shavuot, or that it was ill.

notes.he: דרבי פפייס מאי אתא לאשמועינן דבשלמא אי אמרת דהאי חג סוכות ובעצרת לא הוה חולה אתא רבי פפייס לאפוקי מדרבא אלא השתא מאי שמעינן מיניה:
notes.en: What is his testimony: what does Rabbi Pappeyas come to teach us? Granted, if you say that this ḥag is Sukkot and on Shavuot it was not ill, Rabbi Pappeyas comes to exclude the view of Rava. But now, what do we learn from it?

notes.he: דבשלמא אי לא היה חולה בעצרת והאי חג הסוכות קאתא רבי פפייס לאפוקי דרבא אלא השתא מאי אשמועינן:
notes.en: If so, what is his testimony: granted, if it was not ill on Shavuot and this refers to the festival of Sukkot, Rabbi Pappeyas comes to exclude the view of Rava; but now, what does he teach us?

messages.text: His testimony serves to exclude the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who said that the offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed as a peace offering. Rabbi Pappeyas therefore testifies that the offspring of a peace offering is sacrificed as a peace offering, and that this was the actual practice in the Temple.

notes.he: כיון דמשום הכי לא אקרבוה דחולה הוה הא הוה בריא הוו מקריבי ליה בעצרת א"כ מאי אסהדותיה דרבי פפייס מאי חדוש אשמעינן דקאמר ואכלנוהו בחג דילמא היינו טעמא משום דחולה הוא בעצרת. אלא האי חידוש קמ"ל לאפוקי מדר' אליעזר:
notes.en: If so: since that is why they did not sacrifice it, because it was ill, had it been healthy they would have sacrificed it on Shavuot. If so, what is the purpose of Rabbi Pappeyas’s testimony? What novelty did he teach us in saying “and we ate it on the Festival”? Perhaps the reason is that it was ill on Shavuot. Rather, this is the novelty he teaches us: to exclude the view of Rabbi Eliezer.

messages.text: Mishna

The offspring of a thanks offering and the substitute of a thanks offering, and the offspring of the offspring and its substitute, and the offspring of their offspring until the end of all time, they are all like thanks offerings, with the only difference being that they do not require the accompanying loaves, unlike the thanks offering itself.

notes.he: וקריבין ונאכלין ליום ולילה:
notes.en: MISHNA: These are like a thanks offering: they are sacrificed and eaten for a day and a night.

messages.text: Gemara
From where is this matter derived, that the offspring and substitute of a thanks offering do not require the accompanying loaves?
messages.quote: they do not require the accompanying loaves

messages.text: “If he offers it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mingled with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil” (Leviticus 7:12). What does the term “offer it [yakrivenu]” serve to say?
messages.lead: As the Sages taught in a baraita, with regard to the verse:

verse.he: אִם עַל־תּוֹדָה יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ וְהִקְרִיב ׀ עַל־זֶבַח הַתּוֹדָה חַלּוֹת מַצּוֹת בְּלוּלֹת בַּשֶּׁמֶן וּרְקִיקֵי מַצּוֹת מְשֻׁחִים בַּשָּׁמֶן וְסֹלֶת מֻרְבֶּכֶת חַלֹּת בְּלוּלֹת בַּשָּׁמֶן׃
verse.en: One who offers it for thanksgiving shall offer, together with the sacrifice of thanksgiving, unleavened cakes with oil mixed in—unleavened wafers spread with oil—and cakes of choice flour with oil mixed in, well soaked.

notes.he: אם על תודה יקריבנו והקריב וגו' דהוה [מצי] למכתב (אם על תודה) והקריב על זבח התודה:
notes.en: GEMARA: What does “he shall offer it” say: “If he offers it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer” etc. — since [the verse] could have written: “[If for a thanksgiving,] then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving.”

notes.he: כלומר דהאי יקריבנו דאם על תודה כוליה מיותר דמצי למימר ואם על תודה והקריב על זבח התודה:
notes.en: [What does “he shall offer a thanks offering” say? That is, this “he shall offer it” in “if for a thanksgiving” is entirely superfluous, since it could have said: “And if for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving.”

messages.text: The term is referring to one who designates a thanks offering and it was lost, and he separated another in its place, and then the first animal was found, and now both of them stand before him available for sacrifice. From where is it derived that he may sacrifice whichever one he wants and bring its accompanying loaves with it? The verse states: “He offers a thanks offering,” indicating that he may offer either one.

notes.he: מ"מ:
notes.en: The verse states “he shall offer a thanks offering”: in any case.

notes.he: אלא מה ת"ל יקריב אתה למד למפריש תודתו כו':
notes.en: Rather, what does the verse teach by “he shall offer”? You learn about one who separates his thanks offering, etc.

messages.text: One might have thought that even the second should require the accompanying loaves. Therefore, the verse states: “Offer it,” to teach that only one of them is brought with the loaves, and not two.

notes.he: אם יקריבנו לאחר שהקריב הראשונה:
notes.en: The second: if he sacrifices it after he has sacrificed the first.

notes.he: ומלחם הוא דקא ממעט דאילו מהקרבה לא ממעט לה שניה כדגמרינן להו מאם על תודה דקרבה:
notes.en: “Offer it”: one and not two: it is the loaves that it excludes, since it does not exclude the second from being sacrificed, as we derive [that it is sacrificed] from “if for a thanksgiving.”

messages.text: From where is it derived that the offspring, substitutes, and replacement offerings, in the case where the animal was lost, another was separated in its place, and then the original animal was found, are included and may be sacrificed as well? The verse states: “And if…as a thanksgiving,” teaching that they may all be sacrificed as thanks offerings.

notes.he: להקרבה:
notes.en: From where to include etc.: for sacrifice.

notes.he: כגון אבדה והפריש אחרת תחתיה:
notes.en: And replacements: for example, it was lost and he separated another in its place.

notes.he: צ"ע מה חליפות דאי הפריש תודה ואבדה והפריש אחרת תחתיה ונמצאת הראשונה והרי שתיהן עומדות הא כבר שמעינן ליה מרישא דברייתא:
notes.en: And replacements: this requires further study: what are replacements? For if he separated a thanks offering and it was lost, and he separated another in its place, and the first was found, and both of them stand, we already heard this from the beginning of the baraita.

notes.he: היינו שאבדה והפריש אחרת תחתיה:
notes.en: Replacements: that is, it was lost and he separated another in its place.

notes.he: ריבה דתמורת ולדות וחילופות נמי הוי תודה]:
notes.en: The verse states “And if for a thanksgiving”: it included that substitute, offspring and replacements are also a thanks offering.]

messages.text: One might have thought that all of them require loaves. Therefore, the verse states: “With the sacrifice of thanksgiving,” which indicates that only the thanks offering itself requires loaves, but its offspring and its substitute and its replacement do not require loaves.
Mishna

With regard to the substitute of a burnt offering, the offspring of the substitute, e.g., if one substituted a female animal for a burnt offering, and it gave birth to a male, and the offspring of the offspring of its offspring until the end of all time, they are all like burnt offerings and therefore they require flaying and cutting into pieces and must be burned completely in the fire.

notes.he: כגון המיר זכר בעולה:
notes.en: MISHNA: The substitute of a burnt offering: for example, he exchanged a male for a burnt offering.

notes.he: כגון אם המיר נקבה בעולה וילדה התמורה זכר:
notes.en: The offspring of a substitute: for example, if he exchanged a female for a burnt offering, and the substitute gave birth to a male.

notes.he: תמורת עולה (או) כגון שהומר בעולה זכר תמורה נקבה [וילדה אותה תמורה נקבה]:
notes.en: The substitute of a burnt offering: for example, a female substitute was exchanged for a male burnt offering [and that female substitute gave birth].

notes.he: כלומר ולד תמורה ולד [שילדה] תמורה ולד ולדן עד סוף העולם הרי אלו כעולה ואע"ג דההיא תמורה נקבה דלא חזיא לעולה קדשה (כדתנן) [כדאמר] בפ"ק ממירין מן הזכרים על הנקבות ומן הנקבות על הזכרים:
notes.en: Their offspring [a marginal gloss suggests reading: and the offspring of the substitute that gave birth, the offspring of their offspring, etc.]: that is, the offspring of a substitute, the offspring [that] the substitute [bore], the offspring of their offspring until the end of the world, these are like a burnt offering. And even though that substitute is a female, which is not fit for a burnt offering, it is sanctified, [as was said] in the first chapter: one may substitute males for females and females for males.

messages.text: In the case of one who designates a female animal as a burnt offering, which may be brought only from males, and that female gave birth to a male, although it is a male, it is left to graze until it becomes unfit [sheyista’ev] and then it is sold, and he brings a burnt offering with the money received for its sale.

notes.dh: [המפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה זכר ירעה עד שיסתאב וימכר] ויביא בדמיו עולה
notes.he: לנדבת צבור ומשום הכי ירעה דקא אתי מכח קדושה שאינה ראויה דנקבה לא חזיא לעולה וכ"ש אמו דרועה:
notes.en: [One who designates a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth to a male: it grazes until it becomes unfit and is sold,] and he brings a burnt offering with its money: for communal gift offerings. And for this reason it grazes: because it comes from the power of a sanctity that is not fit, since a female is not fit for a burnt offering, and all the more so its mother grazes.

messages.text: The male offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.he: הולד אל ירעה אלא יקרב עולה:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar says: It itself: the offspring shall not graze but shall be sacrificed as a burnt offering.

messages.text: Gemara

The first clause of the mishna states that the offspring of a female substitute for a burnt offering is brought as a burnt offering, whereas in the latter clause the Rabbis and Rabbi Elazar disagree about the status of a female animal that was consecrated as a burnt offering. What is different in the first clause that they do not disagree, and what is different in the latter clause that they disagree?
messages.quote: they are all like burnt offerings

notes.he: גבי ולד תמורת עולה דלא פליגי רבנן דבדברי הכל קאמר הרי אלו כו' והויין כליל לאישים:
notes.en: GEMARA: What is different: with the offspring of the substitute of a burnt offering, that the Rabbis do not disagree, since it states as the view of all: “these are” etc., and they are completely for the fire.

notes.he: גבי ולד עולה פליגי רבנן דהוא עצמו לא יקריב אלא דמיו:
notes.en: And in the latter clause: about the offspring of a burnt offering the Rabbis disagree, [saying] that it itself is not sacrificed, only its money.

notes.he: דלא פליגי רבנן בתמורת עולה ולד תמורה אלא מודו דהרי אלו כעולה דקרבי:
notes.en: [What is different in the first clause: that the Rabbis do not disagree about the substitute of a burnt offering and the offspring of the substitute, but agree that these are like a burnt offering, which are sacrificed.

notes.he: בהמפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה זכר דפליגי דאמרי ירעה:
notes.en: And what is different in the latter clause: about one who designates a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth to a male, that they disagree, saying it grazes.

messages.text: Even the first clause is taught as a matter in dispute between the Rabbis and Rabbi Elazar, and the ruling there is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar.

notes.he: כשם שחולקין בסוף כך חולקין בראשונה ורישא דקתני הרי אלו כעולה ר"א היא:
notes.en: It is taught as a dispute: just as they disagree at the end, so they disagree in the first clause, and the first clause, which teaches “these are like a burnt offering,” is Rabbi Elazar[’s view].

notes.he: אמר רבה בר בר חנה] במחלוקת שנויה [כמו דפליגי] בסיפא קא פלגי ברישא והאי דתני הרי אלו כעולה רבי אליעזר היא ולא רבנן:
notes.en: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:] It is taught as a dispute: [just as they disagree] in the latter clause, they disagree in the first clause; and what is taught, “these are like a burnt offering,” is Rabbi Eliezer[’s view] and not the Rabbis’. [So Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the daf reads Rabbi Elazar.]

notes.dh: ל"א וכליל לאשים [דברי הכל היא ורמינהי כו'
notes.he: אמר רב הונא במחלוקת שנויה ברישא כך בסיפא וכליל לאשים לא דברי הכל היא אלא לר' אלעזר היא:
notes.en: Another version: “and completely to the fire” [is the view of all, and raise a contradiction, etc. Rav Huna said: It is taught as a dispute; as in the first clause, so in the latter clause; and “completely to the fire” is not the view of all but is Rabbi Elazar’s. [This version names Rav Huna where the daf has Rabba bar bar Ḥana.]

messages.text: You may even say that the first clause is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, but they disagree with Rabbi Elazar only with regard to one who designates a female animal for a burnt offering, as they maintain that the offspring may not be sacrificed because its mother may not be sacrificed. But with regard to the offspring of a substitute, since its mother, i.e., the original burnt offering that is the source of the mother’s sanctity as a substitute, may also be sacrificed, even the Rabbis concede that the offspring may be sacrificed.

notes.he: לאו אימיה ממש אלא הקדש ראשון שבאו אלו כולן מכחו הוא קרב דזכר הוה אבל גבי מפריש נקבה לעולה היא היתה הקדש ראשון ולא קרבה:
notes.en: With regard to the offspring of a substitute, its mother is sacrificed: not its actual mother; rather, the first consecration, by whose power all these came, is sacrificed, since it was a male. But with one who designates a female for a burnt offering, she was the first consecration, and she is not sacrificed.

notes.dh: אבל גבי ולד תמורה דאימיה נמי קרבה
notes.he: לאו אימיה ממש אלא הקדש ראשון שבאו אלו מכחן והוא קרב דזכר הוא:
notes.en: But with regard to the offspring of a substitute, whose mother is also sacrificed: not its actual mother; rather, the first consecration, by whose power these came, and it is sacrificed, since it is a male.

notes.he: לעולה דנקבה היא הילכך קא אמרי בנה ירעה:
notes.en: Since its mother is not sacrificed: as a burnt offering, since it is a female; therefore they say its offspring grazes.

notes.he: דאימיה [דוולד תמורה] דתמורת קרבה ועולה עצמה קרי לה אימיה דתמורה באה מכחה אפילו רבנן מודו דולדן הרי אלו כעולה:
notes.en: But with regard to the offspring of the substitute of a burnt offering: whose mother is sacrificed, [the mother of the offspring of the substitute]; he calls the burnt offering itself the “mother” of the substitute, since the substitute comes from its power. Even the Rabbis concede that their offspring are like a burnt offering.

notes.he: ובתמורת עולה לא פליגי עליה דר' אלעזר דהא תמורת עולה נקבה] שנייה היא להך קמייתא דתמורה היינו שנייה וקמייתא דאפריש [קודם שהפריש התמורה] עיקר עולה זכר הפריש (הילכ') [הילכך] לא קנסו רבנן בולד תמורה אלא אמרי דיקרב:
notes.en: You may even say: and with the substitute of a burnt offering they do not disagree with Rabbi Elazar, since the female substitute of a burnt offering] is secondary to that first one, for the substitute is the secondary one, and the first one, which he separated [before he separated the substitute], was a principal burnt offering; he separated a male. [Therefore] the Rabbis did not penalize the offspring of the substitute, but said that it is sacrificed.

messages.text: And did Rabbi Elazar say that the offspring of a female designated as a burnt offering itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering? But one may raise a contradiction from the mishna (20b):
messages.quote: itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering

messages.text: The substitute of a guilt offering, the offspring of that substitute, and their offspring and the offspring of their offspring, until the end of all time, all graze until they become unfit, and then each animal is sold, and the money received for the sale is allocated for communal gift offerings.

notes.he: ירעו דהלכה למשה מסיני הוא כל שבחטאת מתה באשם רועה ותמורת חטאת מתה:
notes.en: The substitute of a guilt offering: they graze, since it is a halakha to Moses from Sinai: in any case where a sin offering dies, with a guilt offering it grazes; and the substitute of a sin offering dies.

notes.he: לשופרות שקריבין מדמיהן נדבת צבור:
notes.en: For gift offerings: for the horns [the collection chests], from whose money communal gift offerings are sacrificed.

notes.he: וולדן ולד של תמורת אשם ולד ולדה. ויפלו דמיו לנדבה. לשופרות היינו לנדבת צבור:
notes.en: But one who designates a female for a burnt offering, etc. And their offspring: the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering, the offspring of its offspring. And their money goes to gift offerings: to the horns [the collection chests], that is, to communal gift offerings.

messages.text: These animals are not left to graze until they become unfit and then each animal is sold; rather they are left to die.

notes.he: דאית ליה כחטאת כאשם בריש מס' זבחים (דף י:):
notes.en: They die: since he holds [that a guilt offering is] like a sin offering, at the beginning of tractate Zevaḥim (10b).

messages.text: Communal gift offerings are not purchased with the money from the sale; rather, the owner should bring an individual burnt offering with the money received for its sale.

notes.he: דמותרות לנדבת יחיד אזלי:
notes.en: He brings a burnt offering with their money: since surplus goes to an individual’s gift offering.

notes.dh: ר' אלעזר אמר ירעה וימכר ויביא בדמיהן עולה
notes.he: לנדבת יחיד אבל לא יביא בדמיהן אשם כדאמרינן לקמן דמותר אשם לא קרב אשם אלא ירעה ולד דתמורת אשם נמי ירעה ויביא בדמיו עולה [בדמיו יביא הוא עצמו לא יקרב]:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar says: It grazes and is sold, and he brings a burnt offering with their money: for an individual’s gift offering. But he does not bring a guilt offering with their money, as we say below that the surplus of a guilt offering is not sacrificed as a guilt offering but grazes; the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering also grazes, and he brings a burnt offering with its money. [With its money he brings one, but it itself is not sacrificed.]

messages.text: One infers from Rabbi Elazar’s statement that with the money received for its sale, yes, one brings an individual burnt offering, but the offspring of the substitute itself, no, one may not bring it as a burnt offering.
messages.quote: bring an individual burnt offering with the money

notes.he: ולד תמורה לא. אלמא כיון דאימיה לא חזיא להקרבת עולה דאין נקבה קריבה עולה ועוד דאפילו הואי זכר גמירי דתמורת אשם רועה הילכך ולד נמי לא קרב ובולד עולת נקבה אמאי קאמר דקרב:
notes.en: It itself: the offspring of the substitute, no. Evidently, since its mother is not fit to be sacrificed as a burnt offering, as a female is not sacrificed as a burnt offering, and furthermore, even were it a male, it is learned that the substitute of a guilt offering grazes, therefore the offspring too is not sacrificed. Then with the offspring of a female burnt offering, why does he say that it is sacrificed?

notes.he: וא"ת מאי קמ"ל דלמא שאני הכא דלא קרב דכל שבחטאת מתה באשם רועה וולד חטאת מתה ומש"ה באשם ירעה אבל הוא עצמו לא יקרב וי"ל דלא נגמרה באשם רועה אלא בהני דשייכי כהלכתו באשם כגון מתו בעליו או נתכפרו או תמורה או עברה שנתה דכל הני ד' דשייכי באשם כהלכתו אבל ולד אשם דלאו כהלכתו הוא דאשם זכר הוא ולא שייך ביה ולד בהא לא נגמרה ההלכה:
notes.en: With their money, yes; it itself, no: And if you will say: what does this teach us? Perhaps it is different here, that it is not sacrificed, because in any case where a sin offering dies, with a guilt offering it grazes; the offspring of a sin offering dies, and therefore with a guilt offering it grazes, but it itself is not sacrificed. One can say: “with a guilt offering it grazes” was established only for those cases that apply to a guilt offering in its proper way, such as its owner died, or achieved atonement, or a substitute, or its year passed; all these four apply to a guilt offering in its proper way. But the offspring of a guilt offering is not in its proper way, since a guilt offering is a male and offspring does not apply to it; for this the halakha was not established.

messages.text: Rabbi Elazar was speaking to them in accordance with the statement of the Rabbis, as follows: According to me, I hold that even the offspring itself is also sacrificed as a burnt offering. But according to you, who say that the animal is left to graze until it becomes blemished and then it is sold and the money used for the purchase of burnt offerings, concede to me at least that the remainder of the money goes for the purchase of individual gift offerings, rather than communal offerings.
messages.quote: the offspring of the substitute itself, no

notes.he: וא"ת תיקשה מרבנן לרבנן לפי הא דאמר רבא לעיל דהיכא דאימיה קרבה אפילו רבנן מודו דולד נמי קרב והכא בולד תמורת אשם אימיה קרבה א"כ הוה להו למימר דולד עצמו יקרב וי"ל דרב חסדא דהכא לית ליה האי שינויא דרבא דלעיל אלא ס"ל כדמשני רבה בר בר חנה במחלוקת שנויה ור"א היא ורבא דמשני לעיל דהיכא דאימיה קרבה אפילו רבנן מודו משני הכא שינויא אחרינא כדאיתא בסמוך דרבא משני שינויא אחרינא ומורי הרמ"ר פי' דלעולם מצי למימר דרב חסדא נמי אית ליה שינויא דרבא דלעיל דהא דאמר דהיכא דאימיה קרבה אפילו רבנן מודו ה"מ גבי ולד תמורת עולה דעיקר תחילת הקדש קרב עולה ומש"ה דין הוא שיהא הולד עצמו קרב עולה אבל הכא גבי ולד תמורת אשם דעיקר תחילת הקדש קרב אשם ולא עולה אין דין שיהא הולד קרב עולה וה"נ קאמר לר"א במפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה דאין עיקר קרב עולה אלא רועה הולד עצמו קרב הכי נמי ה"ל למימר בולד תמורת אשם ואע"ג דאין עיקר ההקדש קרב עולה הולד עצמו קרב. מורי הרמ"ר:
notes.en: But according to you, who say it is not sacrificed: And if you will say: then there is a contradiction between the Rabbis and the Rabbis, according to what Rava said above, that where its mother is sacrificed even the Rabbis concede that the offspring too is sacrificed. Here, with the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering, its mother is sacrificed; if so, they should have said that the offspring itself is sacrificed. One can say: Rav Ḥisda here does not accept Rava’s answer above, but holds like the answer of Rabba bar bar Ḥana, that it is taught as a dispute and the first clause is Rabbi Elazar’s. And Rava, who answered above that where its mother is sacrificed even the Rabbis concede, answers here differently, as follows shortly, where Rava gives another answer. And my teacher, the RaMaR, explained that Rav Ḥisda can indeed accept Rava’s answer above: when he says that where its mother is sacrificed even the Rabbis concede, that applies to the offspring of the substitute of a burnt offering, where the principal original consecration is sacrificed as a burnt offering, so it is right that the offspring itself be sacrificed as a burnt offering.
